summary.headline: Gala Precision Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to about INR94 crores, EBITDA margin 16.76%, with management guiding 17-19% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was about INR94 crores (+31% YoY), with EBITDA of INR16 crores (+43% YoY, margin 16.76%, +135 bps) and PAT of INR11 crores (+26% YoY, margin 11.31%). For H1 FY27, revenue was about INR169 crores (+26%), EBITDA INR28 crores (+35%, margin 16.56%) and PAT INR19 crores (+26%, EPS INR40.30). Order book grew 44% YoY, crossing INR100 crores in a single quarter. Management reiterated 25% growth for FY27 and an EBITDA margin target of 17-19%, while the Chennai plant and a planned Wada land-based expansion drive capacity additions.

financial_highlights.value: Crossed INR100 crores in a single quarter

segments.name: DSS (disc spring)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 53% of H1 FY27 revenue; management says DSS utilisation is the highest, around 85%, and growth is volume-led.

segments.name: SFS (stud/fastener)
segments.commentary: About 31% of H1 FY27 revenue. Chennai SFS contributed about INR22 crores in H1 FY27 versus INR0.64 crore in H1 FY26; Chennai Phase 1 revenue about INR15 crores in Q2.

segments.name: CSS
segments.commentary: About 16% of H1 FY27 revenue; mainly India-focused, with utilisation said to be slightly lower than DSS.

segments.name: End-user industries
segments.commentary: Renewable energy 42%, industrial 33%, mobility 25% of revenue. Exports about 36% of H1 revenue (management cited 38% in the Q&A).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 25% reiterated; FY28 growth targeted at 25% (management cited 25-30% annual growth).
EBITDA margin target maintained at 17% to 19%, with no major change in the range.

Chennai Phase 2 expected operational by about end-November or January, adding about INR50 crores capacity (taking Chennai to about INR110 crores) in Q4; management said it may pull this forward by one month.

Wada expansion: the 10-acre land deal is expected to be finalised; a new facility is targeted for partial operation in Q4 FY28 with about INR100 crores capacity, taking total capacity from INR450 crores to about INR550 crores, and about INR900 crores over time.
KPMG working-capital diagnosis is complete; implementation planned from early FY28, with benefits taking 1 to 1.5 years.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity is about INR450 crores annual, covering Wada and Chennai; utilisation is about 80-85% company-wide per management.

Chennai fastener plant: installed capacity 4,600 metric tons (high-tensile fasteners); utilisation 35% in FY26, targeted 70% in FY27. Phase 1 capacity about INR60 crores per year (about INR5 crores per month), running near full.
FY28 capex planned at INR40-45 crores, described as year-on-year maintenance and growth capex; land purchases carry higher capex in that year.
Solar plant of about 1.2 MW AC (open access, Nanded, Maharashtra) commissioned on October 30, 2026; capex INR6.2 crores, annual saving about INR1.3-1.35 crores, gross payback about 4.5 years.
Bank finance of INR58 crores secured (INR15 crores fund-based working capital, INR10 crores non-fund-based, INR28 crores term loan); management said the land payment will come from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth was mainly volume-led, from three pillars each contributing about 10%: organic growth, new components from existing customers, and new customers. Q1 included about INR3 crores of held-back dispatches that were recognised in Q2.
Wind: company share of business with most wind OEMs is 5% to 25-30%. Smart fasteners for offshore wind have started exporting; bolts for wind towers are a new product line.

Electrolyzer: first bulk order received in June 2026, with about INR2 crores of FY27 sales expected; advanced sample discussions with two other electrolyzer companies. Railway safety, offshore wind and electrolyzer opportunity estimated at INR40-50 crores of revenue over 2-3 years.
Auto: a European customer (manufacturing in India) approved in July is taking pilot lots in Q3-Q4; RFQ discussions started with other Tier 1s.
Exports: management sees no major change in competitive intensity; growth is driven by new customers and added resources in Europe and the US.
Customer approvals received for critical applications in railway safety, offshore wind and mining equipment, estimated at about INR100 crores of annual customer potential.
Management expects 2026-28 segment mix: renewable 35-38%, industrial 35-37%, mobility about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Wada capacity plan and the MoU for expansion translate into timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10-acre Wada land MoU was signed in June 2026 and legal work is nearly complete; the plan is phased expansion of about INR450 crores, with Q4 FY28 as the target for partial operation, plus rented space as a backup.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 growth like-for-like, and is there any price or inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 included about INR3 crores of dispatches held back from Q1. Growth was mainly volume, with no price-rise split given. On inventory, management said days were about 100-plus, goods in transit are included, and it targets a further 10% cut.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chennai Phase 1 revenue run-rate and utilisation, and does Phase 2 need approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 revenue was about INR15 crores in Q2 and it is running near its INR60 crores annual capacity. Phase 2 adds about INR50 crores with no new approval needed, and ramp-up is expected within 15 days to 1 month of order flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H1 operating cash flow lag profit, and what is the KPMG working-capital plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Export receivables rose because exports grew about INR5 crores and transit time is long; the export working-capital cycle is 90-100 days. KPMG's diagnosis is complete, with implementation planned from early FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the H1 EBITDA margin improvement, and is there guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower manpower costs and other expenses down about 2.2% of revenue, and no forex loss versus H1 FY26; RM cost rose on mix. Guidance is 17-19%, reiterated later in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Chennai base effect: how much H1 growth is organic at Wada?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chennai SFS added about INR22 crores in H1 FY27 versus INR0.64 crore last year, so most of the H1 growth of about INR35 crores came from Chennai; some Wada SFS orders were moved to Chennai.

risks_watch: Working capital: H1 operating cash flow lagged reported profit; receivables and inventory rose, and inventory days are about 100-plus per management.
Capacity constraint: utilisation of about 80-85% company-wide, DSS near 85%, with the Wada expansion and new facility dependent on government approvals and possible delays.
Chennai FY29 expansion: SIPCOT plot applications were unsuccessful; private land of 3-5 acres is being explored.
Wind sector demand flat in India (about 3.1 GW in April-September per an analyst citing reported data), and management's 25% FY27 growth target depends on new customers and product lines.
Employee cost: H1 rose about 0.7% as a share of revenue (per management's statement on the call), with hiring in Europe and the US; management expects this to ease in H2.
Commissioning of Chennai Phase 2 and the new Wada facility, plus FY28 capex of INR40-45 crores.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book and margin targets, though candid on the working-capital drag and on capacity timelines that depend on land and approvals. Some answers were loose or corrected by the analyst's own numbers, including inventory days and H1 growth bases.
key_quotes: Order book grew by 44% year on year, crossing INR100 crores for the first time in a single quarter, reflecting a healthy demand across all key end-user industries.
Broadly, at company level, utilization is approximately 80% to 85% as a mix, where the CSS may be slightly lower side and DSS may be the highest.
Going forward also, our guidance, we still maintain that we are targeting EBITDA margin between 17% to 19%, no major change in that.
